note: Allowed UI exception for mobile and tablet viewing and the removed environment badge. UI_V05_LOCK.json and UI_V051_ADDENDUM.json are not modified; tools/verify-ui-v06.mjs proves the page equals the recorded 0.5.1 markup once the mobile stylesheet is removed and the template edits are reverted. tools/verify-ui-v051.mjs now fails by design (template and page differ from 0.5.1 by these recorded changes).

edits.reason: Safe areas: env(safe-area-inset-*) needs viewport-fit=cover; width=device-width and initial-scale=1 are kept.
NET-12: the header environment badge (globe icon + 내부망) is removed without leaving an empty badge, icon or divider.

stylesheet.scope: Only these rules (checked by tools/verify-ui-v06.mjs): @media blocks for narrow windows, (max-width: N px) with N <= 800, any pointer (the FrameConsole app in a narrow window too); @media blocks with (pointer: coarse) in every query, where every selector (nested @container blocks included) starts with :root:not(.frame-native), so the app (WebView2, html.frame-native) on a Windows touch screen keeps the desktop UI; top-level rules for the html.volume-readonly script hook. A mouse window of 801 px or more matches nothing. Appended after work/player-ui.css by work/build-console.mjs; the 0.6.1 stylesheet follows it and is not part of this record (markupSha256 is the build with --without-0.6.1).

allowedDifferences: Header: the environment badge (globe icon and 내부망) is removed without an empty badge, icon or divider (NET-12); the unused i-globe symbol stays in the icon definitions because UI_V05_LOCK.json lists it.
Viewport meta adds viewport-fit=cover so env(safe-area-inset-*) applies; width=device-width and initial-scale=1 are kept.

Touch screens (pointer: coarse, not the FrameConsole app): about 44 px hit boxes for navigation, toolbar, player buttons, sliders (a 44 px box around the unchanged track and thumb), quality options, chat and dialog buttons, with unchanged icons; 16 px text in fields (no iOS focus zoom); no double-tap zoom on the player; a disabled picture-in-picture button is hidden; the player bar adapts to the player width (labels at 600 px, the volume slider at 500 px, picture-in-picture at 340 px hide), so the fullscreen button stays inside the player.

Narrow windows (800 px or less, any pointer) and touch devices up to 1366 px: the info and chat buttons move from their own row into the right side of the top bar; dialogs keep header and buttons in the visible, safe-area height while the body scrolls; the v0.5 sidebar footer stays hidden in the phone tab bar; tab labels are no longer clipped; content and top bar respect safe-area insets.
Touch tablets (801 to 1366 px) and landscape phones: the 0.5 compact rail (72 px icon sidebar of the expanded view) replaces the 220 px sidebar.

Narrow windows and touch portrait: the player stacked over the chat in the visible height (--frame-visual-height from visualViewport, else 100dvh); the player is 16:9 from 427 px width and 240 px tall below it (picture letterboxed), and lower only where the chat would drop under its minimum height (short window, on-screen keyboard), so the message box and send button stay on screen. Touch landscape (landscape phones of 800 px or less included): the player fills the visible height beside a chat column, also in the expanded view. The picture is always fitted whole (object-fit: contain) and the frame does not move when the controls show or hide. Touch phones: send button beside the message box; landscape phones: 48 px top bar.

Touch screens with little visible height (on-screen keyboard): below 340 px of viewer workspace the chat minimum height drops to 150 px, below 200 px to 100 px and the chat header gives way (the top-bar chat button still closes the chat); the player controls give way where they no longer fit in the player (portrait below 290 px, landscape below 140 px of workspace) and return when the keyboard closes.

Script hooks (set by work/console-ux.js): html.volume-readonly hides the volume slider and keeps the mute button where video.volume cannot change (iOS); #viewer-fullscreen gets the hidden attribute where no fullscreen API exists.

Mouse windows of 801 px or more are unchanged: pixel-identical to the build without 0.6 apart from the removed badge (verification/mobile/results.json, desktopCompare: 801, 1000, 1100, 1440 px and the app on a touch screen).

changes.note: Checker defects 1-7 fixed: landscape phones of 800 px or less (667x375, 780x360) use the side-by-side touch-landscape viewer instead of the stacked one, so the expanded view with chat keeps its controls; the stacked viewer is a flex column whose player shrinks before the chat drops under its minimum (800x700 mouse, 320x568), with low-height rules for the on-screen keyboard; player bar thresholds 600/500/340 px; description of the 240 px minimum corrected; every touch rule scoped to :root:not(.frame-native); stylesheet scope recorded as the real rules (narrow = 800 px or less).
